about: Pooled voice engine 32 voices per track, up to 14 oscillators each Every track keeps a set of ready voices that are reused note after note, the way hardware synths work, so nothing is built while you play.

Sample-exact block timing A note moved by 293 samples: difference 0 Physics and particle devices step in 64-sample pieces counted from the song start, so a note sounds the same wherever the audio blocks fall, live or in an export.
Bit-identical renders Same checksums in every release Render a song twice and you get the same file, to the last bit. Every release checks the demo song against the one before.
Look-ahead scheduler Clock tick every 20 ms Notes are planned a little ahead on a clock in its own thread, which keeps going even when the window is in the background.
Clean preset switch Old sound gone in 13 to 19 ms Change a preset while the song plays: the old sound is gone almost at once and held notes carry on with the new one.
Every note on time 23 instruments: 0 missed, 0 doubled Switching presets in the middle of a song never drops a note or plays one twice.
Sleeping tracks Stopped demo: 22 % of a core down to 3 % Tracks whose sound has died away stop computing and wake at once on a key, a pad or Play.
Background freeze Six heavy tracks: 59 % to 7 % of the audio thread Tracks you are not changing play from a recording made in the background, and come back live the moment you touch them.
Broadcast loudness meter All 44 accuracy checks pass Meter reads LUFS, loudness range and true peak to ITU-R BS.1770-5 and EBU R128.
Oversampled true peak 4x oversampling, 48-tap filter Peaks that fall between samples are found the way the standard asks.
Sidechain Ducker -12.6 dB at the default amount Ducks a track on every hit of another track at audio rate, also in exports.
Mixer cables Up to 5 levels of cables Sends, groups and sidechains are drawn as cables you drag between channels, with the direction spelled out.
Dockable analyser All six in 1.7 ms a frame Spectrum, spectrogram, stereo field, waveform, loudness and correlation in one window you can dock to any edge.
Updates inside the app Installs after 20 s without input Finds, shows and installs updates, and waits until you are not working.
Interface and DAC mode A bit-perfect checklist, automatic sample-rate switching and a measured round trip for your audio interface.
App icons 49 icons in 7 groups Pick the Dock or taskbar icon, and .audiolab files get their own icon on the Mac.

Neural stem splitter 4 or 6 stems, offline after one download; test: 4 s of sound split in about 35 s on one processor core Splits a finished song into vocals, drums, bass and other parts on your own computer, with the HTDemucs v4 network by Meta.

Audio to MIDI on drop On clean test sounds: every note found, timing within 5 ms Drop, copy or paste audio on an instrument track and choose melody, harmony, chord symbols or drums, or split it into stems first and pick the parts.
AI voices Held notes within about 4 cents Make a voice from an example clip of a few seconds; a recording then sings or talks with that voice and keeps its notes.
Checked AI model 47.4 dB match to the original The OpenVoice V2 network runs in its own process in the desktop app, compared against the original model before it shipped.
Voice note editing Steady notes read to 0.08 cents See a recording as notes, like in Melodyne, and move, split, join or correct them. Pitch is found with the YIN method.
Live voice changer 23.5 ms delay; a choir of 8 uses 5.3 % of a core Pitch correction, formant and a choir of up to 8 voices while you sing, with the TD-PSOLA method that keeps the voice natural.
Real physics Energy drift 6e-12 over 60 s In Orbit, balls circle a centre mass under real gravity and their paths play the synth.
Bounces on the beat 7380 landings compared: identical Bounce and Bouncy Notes work out every bounce with a formula, so each ball lands exactly on the song grid.
Clean sub bass Up to 96 overtones, 168.9 dB clean Sub builds its wave from exact overtones, so nothing folds back as noise.
Psy Bass Same output at any block size A saw at twice the sample rate, where every note of a roll is the same to the sample.
Fractal Up to 4000 pulses a second, aliasing -131.9 dB Pulse patterns from slow note lengths up to audio rate, without harsh aliasing.
Particle instruments Up to 192 particles per track in Emit Emit, Vector Grain, Vector FM and Vector Delay turn moving particles into sound, each in its own audio thread.
Live browsing The swap itself takes 0.1 to 0.4 ms Swap an instrument or effect while the song plays, with no gap in the sound.
Preset library 870 presets (451 synth, 419 drums and more) Every preset is rendered and checked: none silent, none clipping, levels matched by measurement.
Glass interface Blur works on 1/16 of the pixels Frosted glass that catches light from the clips behind it, blurred from a ready-made picture to stay light.
Automatic performance Keeps 95 % of the screen rate Measures your screen and picks the richest look that still runs smoothly.
Studio themes 8 themes, 21 fader designs Looks inspired by other studios, with matching faders and meters.
Fast start On screen in 0.20 s The splash is the real loading screen and appears almost at once.
Sharp visualizer 0.47 ms a frame The visualizer stays sharp on high resolution screens at no extra cost.
